geology: Sedimentary (marine) and igneous (e.g. Kola) apatite deposits; phosphorite beds. Carries F in the apatite lattice and trace REE/U.
extraction: Wet process: finely ground rock digested with sulfuric acid; filter off calcium sulfate (phosphogypsum) to leave phosphoric acid. F evolves as SiF4/HF, recovered as H2SiF6; REE recoverable from WPA liquor.
notes: Cross-link hub: sulfuric acid feed ties to ContactProcess; F byproduct (H2SiF6) feeds fluorine chemistry; REE byproduct makes phosphate a secondary rare-earth source. Theoretical F:P2O5 ratio ~0.089.

geology: Bedded marine evaporite deposits (e.g. Saskatchewan, Urals, Zechstein); sylvinite = intergrown sylvite and halite.
intermediate: Amine-float KCl concentrate or pregnant hot brine
extraction: Froth flotation with amine collectors separates KCl from NaCl (~95-96% KCl); OR dissolution-crystallization (hot leach) exploiting steeper KCl temperature-solubility, crystallizing KCl on cooling.
notes: Sylvite = 63% K2O. Flotation tails carry 2.5-3% KCl loss. Alternative beneficiation: heavy-media and electrostatic separation.

geology: Late-stage marine evaporite (most soluble salts); Dead Sea, Qinghai, Zechstein.
extraction: Hot dissolution of crushed carnallite in wash water (~100 C), evaporation, then cooling crystallization (~25 C, vacuum) to drop KCl; MgCl2 stays in mother liquor.
notes: Carnallite = 17% K2O. Energy-intensive dissolution/recrystallization. MgCl2 brine byproduct can feed magnesium chemistry.

geology: Bedded evaporite salt and salt domes; also solution-mined brine and seawater.
intermediate: Purified ~26% NaCl brine (or molten NaCl for metallic Na)
extraction: Chlor-alkali membrane-cell electrolysis of purified brine: Cl2 at anode, NaOH in catholyte, H2 at cathode; cation membrane passes only Na+. Molten-salt Downs cell yields metallic Na + Cl2.
final_product: Chlorine gas + caustic soda (NaOH) + hydrogen; or metallic sodium
notes: TECH-ENABLING. Cl2 feeds PVC/HCl/chlorination (incl. silicon TCS step); NaOH feeds alumina/pulp/soap; HCl loops back. Salt also feeds the Solvay soda-ash process.

geology: Lacustrine evaporite (e.g. Green River WY, Lake Magadi, Beypazari); ~70% Na2CO3 content.
extraction: Calcine crushed trona to decompose sodium sesquicarbonate, driving off CO2 + H2O; dissolve, filter, recrystallize to purified natural soda ash.
notes: Natural route ~30% of world soda ash. Synthetic Solvay route (~70%) uses NaCl + CaCO3 (see soda-ash-synthetic entry).

geology: No ore of its own; feeds are salt brine and limestone.
extraction: Solvay process: brine saturated with ammonia, then CO2 (from limestone calcination) bubbled through to precipitate NaHCO3, which is calcined (~200 C) to Na2CO3; ammonia recovered and recycled.
notes: Dominant (~70%) global route. Cross-links salt (chlor-alkali feedstock) and limestone (CO2 source via calcination).

geology: Evaporite beds; also synthetic phosphogypsum and flue-gas desulfurization (FGD) gypsum.
extraction: Calcination at 150-170 C drives off 1.5 waters: CaSO4·2H2O -> CaSO4·½H2O + 1.5 H2O. Beta form (atmospheric) for board; alpha form (autoclave) for dense high-strength plaster. Harder burn gives anhydrite.
notes: Phosphogypsum from phosphate processing is a synthetic gypsum source; rehydration (setting) reverses the dehydration.

extraction: Calcination ~900 C: CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2. Slaking CaO with water -> Ca(OH)2 (exothermic). With clay in rotary kiln, CaO fuses to Portland cement clinker.
final_product: Quicklime -> slaked lime Ca(OH)2; Portland cement clinker
notes: Calcination CO2 is a feed for the Solvay process. Lime is a cross-cutting reagent (pH control, flux, flotation).

geology: Quartzite, vein quartz, high-purity quartz sand; selected for low Fe/Al/B/P.
extraction: (1) Carbothermic reduction: SiO2 + C (coke/coal/charcoal/woodchips) in submerged arc furnace 1500-2000 C -> MG-Si + CO. (2) MG-Si + HCl over Cu catalyst (fluidized bed) -> TCS (SiHCl3), purified by distillation. (3) Siemens process: TCS + H2 CVD onto heated Si seed rods -> ultra-pure polysilicon; HCl recycled.
notes: TECH-ENABLING Si backbone for solar PV and semiconductors. HCl/chlorine step links to the chlor-alkali chain. Highly energy-intensive.

geology: Metamorphic flake graphite in gneiss/marble/schist; amorphous (vein) also exists.
extraction: Froth flotation to concentrate flake; for anodes spheroidize (round flakes), then chemical purification (acid-alkali-acid: H2SO4/H2O2 -> NaOH -> HCl) and/or thermal purification to >99.9% (ideally >99.98%) C.
notes: Purification raises anode specific capacity (~350 vs ~280 mAh/g). Thermal purification (>2500 C) is the high-purity alternative to acid leach.

geology: Weathering/alteration of feldspar and aluminosilicates; primary (residual) and secondary (sedimentary) deposits.
extraction: Wet processing: blunging, hydrocyclone/centrifuge classification, flotation to separate kaolin from feldspar/quartz, acid (bleach) treatment to remove iron staining, dewatering.
notes: ~48% paper, ~52% ceramics/paint/rubber/other. Forms from feldspar weathering (links to feldspar).

geology: Granite, pegmatite, feldspathic sands; most abundant rock-forming mineral group.
extraction: Multi-stage froth flotation (HF or HF-free) to remove mica, iron minerals, then separate feldspar from quartz; magnetic separation for iron.
notes: Acts as a flux (lowers melting point) in ceramics/glass. Can be co-separated with kaolin in fine-particle flotation.

geology: Metamorphic hard-rock garnet and heavy-mineral beach/alluvial sands.
extraction: Crush, size by screening, gravity (spiral/table) and magnetic separation to clean garnet from other heavy minerals; sized into abrasive grades.
notes: Brief abrasive commodity. Hardness ~7-7.5 Mohs; valued over silica sand for low free-silica dust.

extraction: Dense-media separation to concentrate, then X-ray luminescence or grease-table sorting; optical/laser sorting for recovery.
notes: Brief abrasive entry. Hardest natural material (10 Mohs); synthetic (HPHT/CVD) diamond dominates abrasive supply.
